audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart carried a blanket "Skill" on six of seven rows while the content layer and the packet chart both read Viktor/Viktor/Viktor/Viktor/Malzahar/Malzahar/Viktor.
audit.why: Viktor's Siphon Power shield plus empowered auto wins short trades, and Hextech Ray (12/11/10/9/8s) contests the Voidling shove; the lane only flips at 6 when Nether Grasp is a point-and-click answer, and reverts at two items when augmented Hextech Ray out-ranges you and Gravity Field cancels the channel.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved to match the content layer and the packet chart; whys rewritten to match each new verdict.

audit.why: Spikes are Lost Chapter (shove engine), level 6 Nether Grasp, Liandry's, and Viktor's late augment scaling. Viktor's R Arcane Storm drops from 120s to 80s at rank 3, which is the window that decides late fights.
audit.corrected: Spike text kept; only fabricated ability names replaced.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated Viktor ability names shipped across spikes, whys, early/mid/late and wants.foe: "Death Ray" for E and "Chaos Storm" for R. The decisive interaction — Gravity Field being the one thing that stops Nether Grasp, and Void Shift's CC immunity blocking that stun — was never stated with numbers.
audit.why: Riot's kit file names Viktor E "Hextech Ray" and R "Arcane Storm". Gravity Field is flagged hardCC and Nether Grasp is flagged channel (interruptible — any CC cancels it); Malzahar's passive grants crowd control immunity while up.
audit.corrected: Real names used everywhere; cooldowns field now carries Gravity Field 17s->13s, Hextech Ray 12s and the Void Shift interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: The field exists to hold real numbers; Gravity Field is 17/16/15/14/13 and Hextech Ray 12/11/10/9/8.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both numbers and the Void Shift note.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, under unrelated titles (lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2). report[7].t claimed TP "doubles" something with no source (UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE).
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body explains another; magnitude claims need a number from the kit.
audit.corrected: Both bullets rewritten to their own titles; the magnitude claim replaced with a behaviour statement.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Check it before every step-up. - spell shield (Iron Boundary) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1, 13s maxed — it is the only thing that stops Nether Grasp, so press R after it drops. - Hextech Ray is 12s at rank 1: shove while it is down. - Void Shift is CC immunity, so a full shield eats the stun outright.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Viktor wins by out-ranging your 650 E with Hextech Ray, stunning you out of Nether Grasp with Gravity Field, and scaling past you.

edits.before: Carry by subtraction — every fight starts 4v5 when your R lands; your job is the wave control that makes the fight happen on your timer.
edits.after: Carry by deletion — Nether Grasp on Viktor removes their sustained damage entirely; make the fight happen while his 80-second R is down.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Visions plus Voidlings clear faster than his 12-second Hextech Ray at rank 1 — crash every wave, take the reset, and make his roams cost him minions.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: With Void Shift down you eat the empowered auto and a 17-second Gravity Field with nothing to break it — wait for the shield to tick back.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport standard — TP doubles your shove-tax map game. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport standard — TP turns every crashed wave into a map play. Cleanse answers the Gravity Field stun that cancels your R; Ignite pairs with R kill threats.

edits.before: Viktor holds the early edge. His Q gives him a shield and an empowered auto that wins the short trades you'd like to start, and his E Death Ray matches your waveclear while poking you off your E-spread, so you don't get the free shove this kit usually enjoys. Play safe, farm with W Voidlings, and don't step into his Q range with your shield down. The sub-50% win rate reflects that he simply out-lanes you if you play greedy.
edits.after: Viktor holds the early edge. Siphon Power gives him a shield and an empowered auto that wins the short trades you'd like to start, and Hextech Ray — 12s at rank 1 — matches your waveclear while poking you off your E-spread, so you don't get the free shove this kit usually enjoys. Play safe, farm with Voidlings, and never walk inside his 600-range Q with Void Shift down. At 49.9% he out-lanes greed.

edits.before: Levels 5 and 6 are your window to swing it. Your point-click R suppresses him regardless of his Gravity Field, and your shield and Voidlings eat a chunk of his Chaos Storm burst, so if you all-in before his stun zone is available you win the fight. Use this spike aggressively, because it is the one clear moment the matchup belongs to you.
edits.after: Levels 5 and 6 are your window to swing it. Nether Grasp point-clicks him, and Void Shift's CC immunity means a full shield eats the Gravity Field stun that would otherwise cancel the channel, so all-in while his 15-second W is down and you win. Use this spike aggressively, because it is the one clear moment the matchup belongs to you.

edits.before: The phase reverts to Viktor at two-plus items. His upgraded Death Ray out-ranges and out-clears you, Gravity Field reliably cancels your suppress channel, and his scaling turns him into a kiting hypercarry that out-DPSes your stationary self in extended fights. Late-game, hold Zhonya and QSS-type tools and look to catch him before he ramps, because a farmed Viktor beats you in a straight teamfight.
edits.after: The phase reverts to Viktor at two-plus items. Augmented Hextech Ray out-ranges and out-clears you, Gravity Field cancels your suppress channel unless Void Shift is up, and a 13-second W plus an 80-second Arcane Storm let him kite and out-DPS your stationary body. Hold Zhonya, keep the shield charged, and catch him before he ramps — a farmed Viktor beats you straight up.
